ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, with $O$ in the center, point $C$ is on the arc $\overset{\frown}{AB}$, and $\angle ADC$, $\angle BEC$ are the angles subtended by arcs $\overset{\frown}{AC}$, $\overset{\frown}{BC}$ on the circumference, respectively. If $\angle AOB=110^\circ$ and $\angle ADC=20^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BEC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle AOB=110^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle ADC+\angle BEC= \frac{1}{2} \angle AOB=55^\circ$,\\
since $\angle ADC=20^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle BEC=\boxed{35^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is a circle, with O marked inside the circle as the center; A, D, E, B, C are all on the circumference, and C is located on the lower minor arc from A to B. In the figure, the chords drawn from D to A and C form ∠ADC, and the chords drawn from E to B and C form ∠BEC; they respectively correspond to arcs AC and BC on the circumference. Reasoning: It is known that the central angle ∠AOB = 110°, so the measure of the minor arc AB is 110°. Also because ∠ADC is an inscribed angle intercepting arc AC, and an inscribed angle equals half the measure of the intercepted arc, arc AC = 2 × 20° = 40°. Since C is on the minor arc AB, arc BC = arc AB − arc AC = 110° − 40° = 70°. ∠BEC intercepts arc BC, therefore ∠BEC = 70° ÷ 2 = 35°.
